history.period: Before British rule in Ambala (verify - no firm date)
history.summary: The Ambika Devi Mandir in Ambala City's Old Town (near the Old Civil Hospital) is one of the oldest shrines in Ambala, dedicated to the three goddesses Amba, Ambika and Ambalika. Local belief holds that Ambala derived its name from Goddess Bhawani Ambika - though there is no historical evidence for this (verify). One source dates the temple to 1764, built by Maharaja Gajpat Singh of Jind; the octagonal shrine with a domed roof, known for its faded wall and ceiling paintings, is generally described only as 'pre-British' (date conflict - verify). The address Kumhar Mohalla Rd, Old Civil Hospital Chowk, Bans Bazar, Old Town, Ambala 134003 was corroborated by geocoding.

name: Ambika Devi Mandir
town_description: Ambala is a historic city in northern Haryana, comprising the old Ambala City and the Ambala Cantonment established by the British. A major railway junction on the Delhi-Kalka line, it is known as the 'twin city' of Ambala Cantt and as a commercial and manufacturing centre; the old city retains pre-British temples and bazaars around the Civil Hospital area.

travel.railway: Ambala Cantt Railway Station - about 6-8 km from the old city temple (verify).
travel.road: Near Old Civil Hospital Chowk, Old Town, Ambala; reachable by road from any part of the city (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Navratri (September-October) for the nine-day celebrations, though very crowded.
visitor_information.opening_hours: UNKNOWN (verify) - no published hours found; likely morning-evening darshan like most North Indian temples.
